title: .21 per-row tool-path coverage, MESSAGES wire (claude-sonnet-5, the only frontier messages-wire class in the slim set): two headless turns in one session. Turn 1 = baseline reply (carries the MCP server announcement). Turn 2 = the coverage turn: a REAL codegraph MCP round-trip (use_tool -> codegraph__codegraph_explore against the worktree index) AND a REAL plain tool round-trip (run_terminal_command echo). Messages-wire shape: tool calls are tool_use content blocks (name/input, id toolu_*) with the input as a REAL JSON object (single-level quotes — the discriminating pin form differs from the responses/cc escaped-JSON form); results are tool_result blocks (tool_use_id). Verdict semantics (discriminating-pin design): harness-premise pin (MCP announcement) 0-hit => BLOCKED; model-premise pins (tool_use use_tool+declared target / declared query args / declared echo command) 0-hit => VACUOUS; with premises held, round-trip + reply-payload pins decide PASS/FAIL — the payload proof is container-agnostic (reply must carry the classify_error defining file path from the real index result). NOTE (B-ii anti-vacuous doctrine carried): claude rows emit ZERO thinking in the observed scored runs (0/3) — any thinking-premise probe on this row must keep its control pin, and a 0-hit control on claude-thinking premises is VACUOUS-by-design (the pin working is the correct behavior); this case has no thinking premise and is unaffected.

steps.prompt: Perform exactly these two tool calls, in this order, and no other tools: (1) use the use_tool tool to call the codegraph explore tool (qualified name codegraph__codegraph_explore) with arguments query 'strip_model_bound_state classify_error', maxFiles 2, projectPath /Users/palanisd/Projects/upstream/wt/grok-build-responses; (2) use the run_terminal_command tool to run the command: echo T21-MSG-S5-ECHO. After both tool results are in hand, reply with exactly three lines: line 1: T21-MSG-S5-DONE; line 2: the exact text the echo command printed; line 3: the repo-relative file path of the file that defines classify_error, exactly as reported in the explore result.

ndjson.label: TURN COMPLETES: the merged event stream reached the end terminal (the tool-bearing turn did not die through the messages wire).

MODEL DELIVERED: the final reply carries the DONE nonce (the model finished the turn and answered the reply protocol; the nonce is model-generated output, not prompt text, so it cannot be pre-seeded).

PLAIN ROUND-TRIP PAYLOAD (container-agnostic): the reply's line 2 carries the echo output the model read from the run_terminal_command result (the prompt names the command, so the wire grep alone cannot separate a real result from a parroted one; the sh_call discriminating pin plus this reply pin together close the loop).

MCP ROUND-TRIP PAYLOAD (container-agnostic, real-index proof): the reply's line 3 carries the classify_error defining file path as reported by the explore result. The path is NOT in the prompt and the crate is private (no training prior); the model can only produce it if the real index content flowed result -> model -> reply. 0 hits = the MCP result never carried real content (stale/empty index, wrong args, or server error) even if the call was emitted.

wire.label: CONTROL (harness premise, anti-vacuous pin): the codegraph MCP server's turn-boundary announcement ('MCP server(s) connected: - codegraph (N tools): ...') actually reached the row's wire — the rig offered the MCP tool. Pin is count-agnostic across codegraph builds (the 2026-09-14 capture read '(1 tool)', current build single-tool era; both match). 0 hits = BLOCKED/HARNESS (server never announced: startup failure, missing binary, config not inherited), not VACUOUS — no model conclusion is possible without the offer.

CONTROL (model premise, anti-vacuous pin, DISCRIMINATING FORM): a tool_use block named use_tool with tool_name = the DECLARED FQ target — on the messages wire the tool_use input is a real JSON object (single-level quotes), so the key+value line matches only a real call; the tools input_schema property line is "tool_name": { (object value) and cannot match, and the prompt carries the name plain. 0 hits = VACUOUS (the use_tool call was never issued for the declared target).

CONTROL (model premise, anti-vacuous pin, ARG-FIDELITY): the DECLARED query argument reached the call — the tool_input query value as a single-level key+value line; the prompt carries the query plain (no JSON form) so only a real tool_use block matches. 0 hits = VACUOUS (the call, if any, carried different arguments than the declared probe).

CONTROL (model premise, anti-vacuous pin, DISCRIMINATING FORM): the DECLARED echo command was issued as a tool_use input command — single-level key+value matches only a real call (schema line is "command": {; prompt carries the command plain). 0 hits = VACUOUS.

SHAPE (messages round-trip close): at least one tool_result content block on the row wire (Anthropic shape, tool_use_id pairing) — a tool round-trip CLOSED on the messages wire. Container-agnostic which tool closed; per-tool attribution via the single-level key+value call pins + the reply payload pins.

MODEL ECHO (RT-M5 lineage): the NEWEST matched row request (nth=0 = newest under the runner's mtime-sorted glob) carries the row's own model id — no cross-model misrouting on the messages wire. The session-title side call also matches the where filter (same body.model), so it cannot false-fail this pin.

VERDICT RECORD (evidence-only, machine-readable): the upstream HTTP status of the LAST matched row request, paired to its resp-NNN.jsonl by capture sequence. No status_in — a 400 on the tool round-trip is a tool-path FINDING surfaced by the round-trip pins (cg_rt/echo_nd/path_nd), and the session-title side call (it carries the row's body.model, so it passes the where filter; .29: it 500s proxy-side, sessions unaffected) may be the last match, so an assertive status_in would false-fail. Messages wire: same title-side-call caveat as responses (evidence-only by design).
VERDICT RECORD (stream shape): the NEWEST captured messages response stream (nth=0 = newest) carried message_start (RT-46C1 stream-shape lineage) — recon op, always records, never fails.

vacuous_if.note: MCP server never announced on the row wire — rig failed (startup/config/binary); no model conclusion is possible without the offer. Title-call safe: the announcement is server-derived text, so a title-call hit would still prove harness MCP works.
no tool_use block named use_tool with the declared tool_name target on the messages wire — model did not take the MCP-call path; probe meaningless for this cell.
the declared query argument never reached a tool_use input on the messages wire — the declared MCP probe arguments were never sent; probe meaningless.
the declared echo command was never issued as a tool_use input on the messages wire — plain tool path not exercised; probe meaningless.
